newsitem.title: USA: GM's Saturn unit exceeded targets in 1996.
newsitem.headline: GM's Saturn unit exceeded targets in 1996.

text.p: General Motors Corp's Saturn division exceeded GM's financial targets in 1996 despite a modest reduction in sales last year, a top executive said Friday.

Joe Kennedy, vice president for Saturn sales, service and marketing, declined to say if Saturn earned an operating profit for the year, but he said the automaker managed to exceed GM's ever-tightening financial targets for the fourth year in a row.

Speaking to Reuters at the Los Angeles Auto Show, Kennedy said Saturn sold about 278,535 cars in the United States last year, down about 2.5 percent from the previous year. He attributed the decline to softer sales in the last two months of the year, but he said sales have already started to perk up again since Christmas.
Kennedy said Saturn's factory in Spring Hill, Tenn. produced 314,000 cars last year, up from 302,500 in 1995. Some of those cars were shipped to Canada and Taiwan.
He said a strike at a GM parts factory earlier this year cost Saturn about 12,000 to 13,000 cars in lost production.
Saturn, the import-fighting division of GM, has been under pressure to earn a profit after GM spent about $5 billion to launch the company.

Saturn officials said the company hopes to increase sales this year, particulalry overseas, as it starts offering cars in Japan. Saturn expects to start selling cars in Japan in April through 14 dealerships. By the end of the year, Saturn hopes to have as many as 20 dealerships selling cars in Japan.
